---
title: "Build a plugin with your coding agent"
sidebarTitle: "Quickstart"
description: "Start a Neovim plugin on Agent SDK by giving your coding agent one prompt, then describing what you want it to build."
keywords: ["quickstart", "plugin", "coding agent", "prompt", "claude code"]
---

The quickest way to build on Agent SDK is to hand the docs to your coding agent and tell it what you want.

<Steps>
  <Step title="Set up an adapter to develop with">
    Your plugin uses whichever adapter your user names, so you need one of your own to try it. See [Installation](/installation#set-up-an-adapter-to-develop-with).
  </Step>
  <Step title="Give your agent this prompt">
    Paste it into Claude Code, or any coding agent:

    <Prompt description="Build a Neovim plugin on Agent SDK" actions={["copy"]}>
    I want to build a Neovim plugin that talks to LLMs and agents using agent-sdk.nvim.

    Read the full documentation at https://agent-sdk.olimorris.dev/llms-full.txt before writing any code. Then:

    - Take an `adapter` option from the user, with no default. Resolve it with `sdk.adapter()` when a conversation starts
    - Never configure adapters or credentials in the plugin
    - Write the plugin so it works on HTTP adapters and ACP agents alike, with a permission handler for agents
    - Test it with the scripted test adapter, so the tests need no network or API keys

    The plugin should:
    </Prompt>
  </Step>
  <Step title="Describe what you want to build">
    Finish the prompt with what your plugin should do. For example:

    - Open a chat buffer, stream each reply into it, and let me stop a reply with `<C-c>`
    - Explain the visual selection in a floating window
    - Review my staged diff and list the problems in the quickfix list
    - Write a commit message from my staged changes
  </Step>
  <Step title="Try it">
    Set up your plugin in your config with the adapter from the first step, then run it:

    ```lua
    require("your_plugin").setup({ adapter = "claude_code" })
    ```
  </Step>
</Steps>
